champion: Systemic mastocytosis with associated hematologic neoplasm
ordered_diagnoses: Systemic mastocytosis with associated hematologic neoplasm

s1.syndrome_frame: a chronic skin condition characterized by asymptomatic red to brown macules and papules with a symmetric distribution on the trunk and extremities
salient_findings: red to brown macules and papules on trunk and extremities
key_facts: male patient in his 20s
12-month history of skin lesions
lesions initially appeared on trunk and spread to upper and proximal lower extremities
lesions were symmetrically distributed and did not coalesce
face, distal extremities, and mucous membranes were unaffected
some lesions resolved spontaneously with residual hyperpigmentation
hypereosinophilia (4220/μL)
elevated tryptase (33.7 ng/mL)
elevated vitamin B12 (>6000 pg/mL)
negative serologic tests for HIV, hepatitis A, B, and C
negative tests for parasitic infections
skin biopsy showed nodular infiltration of histiocytes with lymphocytes and eosinophils
bone marrow analysis showed hypercellularity with myeloid hyperplasia and increased eosinophils

s4.champion: Systemic mastocytosis with associated hematologic neoplasm

raw.champion: Systemic mastocytosis with associated hematologic neoplasm
raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of skin lesions, hypereosinophilia, elevated tryptase, and elevated vitamin B12, along with the bone marrow analysis showing hypercellularity with myeloid hyperplasia and increased eosinophils, and the presence of the FIP1L1-PDGFRA fusion gene, are all consistent with systemic mastocytosis with an associated hematologic neoplasm, likely a myeloproliferative neoplasm.

rejected.label: Mastocytosis
rejected.why: While the patient has some features of mastocytosis, the presence of the FIP1L1-PDGFRA fusion gene and the bone marrow findings suggest a more complex diagnosis.

rejected.label: Erdheim-Chester disease
rejected.why: The patient's lack of lipid-laden foam cells or multinucleated giant cells on skin biopsy and the absence of other typical Erdheim-Chester disease features make this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
rejected.why: The patient's skin biopsy showed nodular infiltration of histiocytes, but the immunohistochemistry results (CD1a negative) do not support Langerhans cell histiocytosis.

rejected.label: Mastocytosis with eosinophilia
rejected.why: While the patient has both mastocytosis and eosinophilia, the presence of the FIP1L1-PDGFRA fusion gene and the bone marrow findings suggest a more specific diagnosis of systemic mastocytosis with an associated hematologic neoplasm.
